regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant when anthracyclines are unsuitable, or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues. In this regimen it is the only take-home chemotherapy tablet; methotrexate and fluorouracil are given in the unit. Methotrexate: Methotrexate reduces the supply of building blocks needed to make DNA. Kidney function affects its clearance, and fluid collections can prolong exposure. In CMF it is given intravenously by the unit; it is not a take-home weekly tablet. Fluorouracil (5-FU): Fluorouracil interferes with DNA and RNA production. In CMF it is given by injection in the unit. DPD testing helps identify increased toxicity risk; it does not exclude all serious reactions.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This dose-dense AC–taxane sequence adds trastuzumab for HER2-positive high-risk early breast cancer. Trastuzumab starts after AC. Fitness, recurrence risk, heart health, nerve symptoms and available HER2-directed alternatives affect selection.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: HER2-positive neoadjuvant or adjuvant high-risk breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Doxorubicin: Doxorubicin interferes with enzymes and DNA processes needed for cell division. It can also affect heart muscle, so the team considers previous exposure and cardiac risk. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues. Paclitaxel: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues. Trastuzumab: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Four AC cycles every 14 days, then four fortnightly paclitaxel treatments with trastuzumab weekly on Days 1 and 8 of each 14-day block (eight weekly antibody doses). Trastuzumab then continues every 21 days to complete one year total; it is not given with AC.

Famotidine may be omitted under the consultant/local plan if appropriate. A prior reaction requires a separate rechallenge assessment; do not reuse the standard draft automatically.
Trastuzumab formulation and observation instructions remain separate from taxane premedication.
Growth-factor support during weekly paclitaxel is individualised; do not automatically carry the mandatory dose-dense AC prescription into this phase.
Confirm IV versus locally approved SC trastuzumab. SC is fixed 600 mg every 21 days without a loading dose; IV and SC missed-dose instructions are different.
No routine chemotherapy antiemetics or paclitaxel premedicines carry into trastuzumab-only continuation. Review previous symptoms/reactions individually.
Continue the cardiac-monitoring clock and confirm the prescribed route, interval and missed-dose rules.
patient_education: Follow the prevention and rescue instructions prescribed for this schedule. Call if vomiting prevents drinking.
Know the local urgent-contact number. Fever, shivering, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs prompt advice even between visits.
Show the oncology pharmacist all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines. Ask before starting anything new.
Paclitaxel reaction medicines and AC anti-sickness medicines have different purposes. They are not automatically continued during trastuzumab-only treatment.
special_support: Paclitaxel weekly for 12 doses with trastuzumab every 3 weeks; continue trastuzumab to complete one year of HER2 treatment when appropriate. The team selects IV trastuzumab or locally approved subcutaneous trastuzumab; these are alternative formulations, not additional medicines.

baseline: Baseline blood tests and review before each chemotherapy administration according to the source and local plan. Once chemotherapy ends, testing follows trastuzumab and individual clinical needs.

Assess cardiac function before trastuzumab and every 12 weeks during treatment. Keep the same monitoring clock when paclitaxel ends or trastuzumab changes schedule; arrange earlier review for symptoms or falling function. EMA product information recommends cardiac checks every 6 months after treatment until 24 months; following anthracyclines in early disease, yearly up to 5 years from the last trastuzumab dose or longer if function falls. Your team individualises this plan.

practical_workflow: Blood tests, medicines review and the consent discussion come first. Confirm baseline and planned ongoing cardiac assessment.

A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.
Paclitaxel is an IV infusion. Trastuzumab may be IV or, if locally approved and prescribed, a subcutaneous injection. Staff confirm formulation, observation and access needs at every phase change.
This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.
observation_and_access: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.
First visits can take longer because of loading doses, premedicines and observation. Ask the unit about expected time, transport and any escort needed after sedation or line insertion.

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 406 treated; resected HER2-positive tumours ≤3 cm, initially node-negative; an amendment allowed one micrometastatic node.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Single-arm phase II: weekly paclitaxel + weekly IV trastuzumab for 12 weeks, then weekly or three-weekly trastuzumab to complete one year.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: NCCP 00512 and 00815 remain node-negative indications. 00815 uses three-weekly IV or locally approved SC trastuzumab during combination: an NCCP adaptation, not the exact APT combination schedule.
evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: 10-year recurrence-free interval was 96.3% (95% CI 94.3–98.3); breast-cancer-specific survival was 98.8% (97.6–100). These endpoints differ from iDFS and OS.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Balance efficacy with the regimen’s drug-specific toxicity, cardiac/organ monitoring and treatment burden; see the source-linked assessment and monitoring sections.
